sourceBindings.text: A digital number is useful only when the sample, preparation method, calibration and stable reading are known. You will rehearse the source's 20 g to 20 mL process card, compare it with a separate manufacturer's method, and measure real samples only under a trainer using the actual meter's documented procedure.

Under trainer observation, prepare an identified soil suspension with the mass, liquid volume, ratio basis and timing of one declared method; keep the source card's 20 g + 20 mL worked example separate from a different manufacturer's protocol.

Calibrate the actual meter with suitable buffers according to its manual, protect the electrode and buffers from contamination, place the sensing area correctly and wait for an accepted stable reading.

Measure and record the actual pH of samples A, B and C with sample and method identities, and recognize a failed calibration, unstable display or implausible result that requires a check or targeted repeat.

sourceBindings.text: First sort three complete preparation cards without mixing values. For the source card, sequence PPE and sample ID, gentle crush, 2 mm sieve, 20 g soil, 20 mL distilled water, one-minute stir, 15-minute stand, manufacturer-directed buffer calibration, careful electrode placement, stable reading and recorded result. At an error screen, choose to stop and troubleshoot. Three blank A/B/C records require learner observations rather than the model key.

Trainer records the real meter/probe/manual and approved site method. Each learner personally prepares the required sample, calibrates and checks the meter, measures A/B/C, records quality and result, rinses and stores the probe, and is observed against every applicable criterion. If the site method differs from the source card, keep the source card as a comparison and update the task sheet before scoring.

sourceBindings.text: soil suspension or slurry
Soil mixed with a declared liquid by a declared mass-to-volume method for measurement.
1:1 g:mL
In the source card, 20 g soil mixed with 20 mL water; the units must stay with the ratio.
buffer
A solution of known pH used to calibrate or check the meter, following the meter's accepted buffer set.
electrode junction
The reference contact that must be positioned and maintained according to the probe manual for a reliable reading.
stability indicator
The meter's sign or site rule that a displayed value has settled sufficiently to record.
quality check
A documented test of whether the calibration, sample preparation and reading are fit for the intended purpose.
